name: progress
title: Progress
description: Displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task.
docs:
## When to use - Work with a measurable end: an upload, an import, a multi-step build. - Work long enough that the user would otherwise wonder whether anything is happening, and short enough that they will watch the bar. - A determinate value next to other numbers, where the bar is a second reading of the same fact. ## When not to use - Work of unknown duration. Pass `value={null}` for an indeterminate bar, or use `spinner` when there is no bar to fill. - A page that is simply loading its own content; use `skeleton`. - A value that is not progressing toward an end, like a score. Render the number. ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/progress ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Progress } from "@/components/cadence/progress/progress"; export function Upload() { return ; } ``` `value` is required and may be `null` for indeterminate work. `Progress` renders its own track and indicator; `ProgressLabel` and `ProgressValue` go inside it as children. ## Examples ### Labelled, with the number ```tsx
Uploading assets
``` `ProgressValue` formats the value with `Intl.NumberFormat`; pass `format` or `locale` to the root to change it. ### Indeterminate ```tsx ``` The fill fills the track and pulses. There is no sweep: a moving gradient says "indeterminate" with motion alone, which is exactly the anti-pattern in the motion system. ### Custom range ```tsx ``` `ProgressValue` renders `60%` for `3/5`; use `getAriaValueText` if you want "step 3 of 5" announced instead. ### Composed track ```tsx ``` Composing the track yourself replaces the default one. The indicator still reads the value from the root, so it keeps animating. ## API ### `Progress` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | | `value` | `number \| null` | – | Required. `null` means indeterminate. | | `min`, `max` | `number` | `0`, `100` | Range. | | `format` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | – | How `ProgressValue` formats the number. | | `getAriaValueText`| `(value, raw) => string` | – | Human-readable value for assistive tech. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last; the default is a wrap layout. | ### `ProgressTrack`, `ProgressIndicator`, `ProgressLabel`, `ProgressValue` Plain wrappers over Base UI's parts; each forwards `className` and native props. `ProgressIndicator` carries the motion. ## Motion contract Recipe: `data.transition`, in both of its documented forms. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------- | | value change | `scaleX old → new` (one-shot) | `data.transition`| yes | | indeterminate | `opacity` pulse (continuous) | `data.transition`| yes | | reduced | value jumps; pulse kept, opacity only | `data.transition` | yes | | none | no transition, `animate-none` | – | – | The fill is a `scaleX` transform on an element that keeps the full track width, so a value change never triggers layout. Under `reduced` the fill jumps to the new value — position is information, the animation is not — while the indeterminate pulse survives, because opacity-only loading feedback is what M5 keeps. ## Keyboard interactions No keyboard interaction: the progress bar is not focusable. If the user can cancel the work, put a `button` next to it. ## Accessibility - Base UI puts `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuenow` on the root; `value={null}` omits `aria-valuenow`. - Give it a name with `aria-label`, or render `ProgressLabel` inside the root and let Base UI wire it. - Announce completion outside the bar (text or `toast`); a full bar is not announced by a screen reader on its own. - Never hide the percentage behind the animation: `ProgressValue` is the readable copy of the same fact. ## Responsive behavior The bar fills its container and stays 8px tall at every breakpoint. When it sits in a card header, keep the label and value on one line and let the bar take the next line — the default `flex-wrap` layout does this without extra classes. ## Performance One Motion element. A determinate update animates a transform; an indeterminate bar runs a CSS opacity loop that the compositor owns, so a page with several bars does not schedule main-thread frames. Avoid driving `value` from `requestAnimationFrame` yourself; pass the real value and let the transition smooth it. ## Notes for AI - `value` is required; pass `null` for indeterminate, never `undefined`. - Use `scaleX`, not width. A width transition relayouts the track every frame. - For work with no measurable end and no bar, use `spinner`, not a fake percentage.
